transcript.text: f/f freezer keeps icing up bottom drawer wont shut proper, defrosted it 2wks ago already full of ice again. indesit

Ice returning within two weeks is not normal. If it is mainly collecting beneath the drawers, the most likely cause is a blocked or frozen defrost drain: defrost water cannot escape, refreezes in the bottom and eventually stops the drawer shutting. A solid ice block on the rear freezer wall instead points more to an automatic defrost fault, such as the defrost heater, sensor/thermostat or control. Please tell me which pattern you have; that will determine whether a careful drain clear after a full defrost is worth trying, or whether it is likely to need an engineer.
its mostly round the front edge and bottom drawer, thick frost. not a solid block on the back wall as far as i can tell

That pattern still fits a blocked or refreezing defrost drain best: meltwater collects at the base, freezes around the front of the bottom drawer and stops it closing. A poor door seal is the other common cause, because moist room air then creates thick frost around the front rather than a solid rear-wall ice block. With the freezer switched off, check the rubber door seal all the way round, especially the lower edge: look for a split, a gap, food/ice holding it open, or a section that has come loose. If the seal looks sound, it is likely to need another full defrost followed by clearing the drain channel/hole with warm water; if ice returns quickly after that, an engineer should investigate the drain arrangement or defrost system.
[Helpful to see: image "Fridge not cooling — simple checks first" — Before suspecting the sealed system, check the temperature setting, that the door seal closes cleanly, that there's air space and clean condenser coils at the back, and listen for the compressor. Unplug before cleaning at the back. A sealed-system or refrigerant repair is a job for a qualified engineer. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
ok checked the freezer door seal, bottom corner is split about 5cm and the hinge side bottom bit is flattened. paper slides straight out there, grips everywhere else

The split seal and failed paper test are enough to explain the rapid frost build-up: warm, damp kitchen air is getting in at the bottom hinge-side corner and freezing around the drawer. The freezer door seal/gasket is therefore the most likely faulty component; the flattened section will not reliably recover if it is also split. Before treating it as the seal alone, check whether the door has dropped or is loose on its hinges, as that can stop even a new seal meeting properly. Remove the ice with a full defrost and dry the cabinet, but it will probably return until the damaged seal is renewed and any door alignment issue is corrected.
door looks straight, not sagging, hinges seem fine. so just need a new seal? what do i search for, i can fit it myself

Search using “Indesit [full model number] freezer door seal” or “freezer door gasket”; the full model number is important, as seals that look similar are often different sizes and fixing types. It can be a DIY job if it is a removable push-in seal: switch the appliance off and unplug it, then the old seal normally pulls out of its retaining groove and the new one presses in. Some seals are bonded or welded to the door instead; those are not a straightforward seal-only replacement and may need an engineer or, in some cases, a door assembly. Do a full defrost and dry-out before fitting any replacement, otherwise the existing ice will keep the drawer from shutting properly.
ok model is IB55532W, will search that. not sure yet if its push-in or screwed, will look closer when i do the defrost. thanks

IB55532W is the right model reference to use in your search, but check the fixing style before choosing a seal: similar-looking gaskets are not interchangeable. The split plus the failed paper test at the flattened hinge-side corner makes the door seal the clear leading cause of the frost, especially as the door itself appears straight. During the full defrost, dry the door and gently lift one corner of the gasket: a push-in type sits in a groove, while some are retained under a strip or by screws; do not force it. Also clear any meltwater from the base while it is defrosted—if ice returns after the seal is sealing properly, the next likely issue is a drain that is blocking or freezing.
